blocks.c: I did not use the key.
I want that understood, because everything after this makes me look like an idiot, and I would like at least one chapter where I am not.
I photographed the key in place. I photographed the bracket. I wrote it in the log:
03:14 B2 — small brass key taped under extinguisher bracket, paper tag reads SORRY. Left in place, photographed. Recommend day shift investigate.
Then I finished the walk, went home, slept badly, and came back at ten the next night.

Not crossed out. Not amended. The page had my 01:00 entry and my 05:00 entry and between them, where three lines of my handwriting had been, there was nothing — not a gap, not a scrape, just the next line where the previous line ended. The way a page looks when you never wrote on it.
I checked my phone. The photographs were there. Two of them, timestamped 03:14, showing a brass key with a paper tag against grey painted steel.
I went down to B2 and put my hand under the bracket and the key was gone.
That should have been the end of it. Key gone, entry gone, I write it up in the morning and let somebody with a salary worry about it.

Here is the thing about doing nights alone in a building for fourteen months. You develop a relationship with it. Not a friendship. More like the relationship you have with a difficult coworker: you know its noises, you know what it does when the weather changes, you know which of its complaints are real.
And I knew, standing on B2 at ten past eleven with my hand under an extinguisher bracket, exactly the way you know when someone has been in your apartment, that the building had taken something back.
I went to the freight car. I got in. I looked at the brass panel.
There was a new button under B2.
It was round, and worn concave, and it had no number on it at all.
